description: Round stainless steel eatery table with a pressed sheet top, folding tubular frame and adjustable feet

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Round stainless steel outdoor eating table, pressed sheet top with a rolled rim, four splayed tubular steel legs cross-braced under the top, plastic foot caps Materials: brushed stainless steel, water-spotted and slightly dented, scuffed chrome legs, rust freckles at the foot caps.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: All four axes measured, not estimated, and none is near a ceiling by accident: 1184/2000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries. The two tight axes were designed in the blockout rather than optimised into at the end -- two macro components and zero repetition systems IS two draw calls, and the 4-fold frame repeat is a construction loop inside one merged buffer rather than four meshes. The dark foot caps ride on the frame material as a vertex-colour split, which is what keeps materials at 2 instead of 3. Both geometries carry a colour attribute, so neither can render black under a vertexColors material.

featureReviews.notes: Disc-on-cage silhouette correct at all four azimuths; turntable ratios 1.0 / 0.9942 / 0.9925 / 0.9938 against a 0.15 collapse floor. Built envelope 0.596 x 0.750 x 0.596 m against the corrected declaration of 0.60 x 0.75 x 0.60 (built aspect 0.795 vs the proxy's measured 0.811, 2% under).

Four vertical legs on the measured 0.294 m square, 28 mm tube, flanged caps, square brace ring. Ring CORRECTED from the proxy's 0.310 m to the plate's 0.500 m after a calibrated re-measurement; that was the one real structural defect and it is fixed. Held back from higher only by the leg-to-top join, which one high-angle view cannot show and the merged proxy cannot resolve (confidence 0.35, authored as a plain socket and declared as an assumption).

Rolled rim and the inset concentric groove both present and reading in the render. The lathe SEAM that split the rim with a 31-level luma step at azimuth 0 (245->214 at y=258, reversing to +27 at y=266) is fixed by welding the first and last radial normal columns; the same scan now reads 226/229/224 with no step.

Neutral satin steel with the plate's 34-level blue cast correctly discarded as open-sky illumination rather than albedo. Darkest element (foot cap at azimuth 270) renders 86.3, clear of the hole gate's ~58 band, vindicating the lift from the measured luma 42. Metalness 0.35 rather than a physical 0.9 because the harness binds no environment map, matching the kit's own shipped stainless convention. Scored 0.74 on first assessment for the top face reading 233.7 against the plate's 117; RE-SCORED to 0.78 after measuring the plate's own rim-to-top ratio, which is 1.15 on the sunlit front and 0.94 on the shaded left -- i.e. that relationship is LIGHTING, not albedo, so the single-tone top is correct and the brightness is the review rig's key light, not a material error. A candidate rim-vs-top vertex tint was tested against that measurement and REJECTED as a fabricated difference. The one real remaining gap is the radial spun brush, which is anisotropy this pipeline cannot emit and which is declared as an omission, not approximated.

name: Stainless Steel Noodle Shop Table
nameTh: โต๊ะสแตนเลส
notes: The ubiquitous Thai street eatery and food-court table. Empty top: nothing on it, no cloth, no condiment caddy. Silhouette is a thin disc on a four-leg tubular frame, so keep the tabletop a single closed slab rather than a shell -- an eatery table is only ever seen from standing height and above. DIAMETER CORRECTED FROM THE PROXY BEFORE BUILDING: the list-time declaration was 0.75 x 0.75 x 0.75, an aspect of 1.0, but the Meshy proxy measures bbox w/h = d/h = 0.811 with a square plan. Height is the trustworthy axis (a dining-height table is 0.72-0.75 m), so diameter = 0.75 x 0.811 = 0.608 -> 0.60 m, which is also a standard round-table size. The proxy also refutes two plate-only readings: the legs are VERTICAL, not splayed (the occupancy columns hold the same x and z in every row from y/H 0.00 to 0.90), and the brace ring sits at y/H 0.41 = 0.31 m above the floor rather than a third below the top. Four legs on a square of side 0.293 m; 28 mm tube; flanged foot caps ~55 mm across.
